executive_summary: Late-cycle easing: tilt toward defensive growth while keeping the core funds.
Health care is the expansion sector; Phase 3 proposes MRK BUY at starter size.
SPMO is added on momentum and cost; JPM is trimmed after the Devil's Advocate damaged its thesis.
PG is held: the staples head rebutted a broken Devil's Advocate verdict.
Technology stays above the macro cap through the core funds (documented override).

reconciliation.phase1_position: Keep technology near 24.4% despite the 20% macro cap.
reconciliation.findings: Fund verdicts: QQQ HOLD, SPMO ADD; overlap between the funds is moderate.
reconciliation.resolution: Tolerate the excess (override kept) and allow the small SPMO add.

reconciliation.phase1_position: Raise health care to 8.2% through Phase 3 stock picking.
reconciliation.findings: Phase 3 produced 1 BUY (MRK) and passed JNJ, ISRG, ABBV.
reconciliation.resolution: Initiate MRK at the starter size; the final target is 7.1%, the rest of the gap stays in cash.

reconciliation.findings: The staples head held KO and PG (PG (SELL -> HOLD)).
reconciliation.resolution: Defer the staples reduction; keep the current weight and re-test after the next filings.

reconciliation.findings: The financials head returned JPM TRIM and BRK-B HOLD.
reconciliation.resolution: The JPM trim delivers the reduction; final target 21.9%.

final_actions.note: Final sector targets leave headroom for the add step.

constraint_overrides.justification: Technology exposure comes entirely through the QQQ and SPMO core funds; cutting it to the macro cap would mean selling core funds at a taxable gain, so the excess is tolerated and reviewed again next run.

top_risks: A growth scare would hit financials and the technology-heavy funds together.
The new health care position depends on pipeline delivery before a patent expiry.
Fund overlap concentrates exposure in a handful of mega-cap names.
Open litigation and regulatory items flagged by OSINT could resurface.
dissent_summary: The Devil's Advocate broke the PG thesis and damaged JPM, ABBV, ISRG; the staples head rebutted the broken verdict and held. Bearish fundamental reads on JPM and on expensive health care finalists were reflected in the TRIM and PASS outcomes. No dissent changed a final action.
conviction_reason: Most findings agree with the Phase 1 direction; sizing is conservative.
